book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind

chapters.file: ch03 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy.md
ch04 - Popular Culture and Philosophy.md
ch05 - AN EXTRAORDINARY GENIUS FOR MINUTIAE.md
ch06 - The House that Holmes Built.md
chapters.relation: Kate Rufa reads Holmes as Spinoza's 'just man': Watson's 'calculating machine' verdict in The Sign of the Four, his unshaken calm while baiting Moriarty before the Reichenbach leap in 'The Final Problem', and the geometric 'Book of Life' of A Study in Scarlet all show passion mastered by reason into adequate ideas and true freedom. The twist is the cocaine: shooting up between cases means Holmes sacrifices his conatus (the striving to persist in being) to keep his mind at a godlike pitch of activity, a God-complex no finite mode can sustain. Moriarty, equally rational but ruled by passive affects, is the shadow of this ideal, echoing Socrates' Apology point that harming others inevitably harms oneself.

chapters.file: ch07 - His Work Is Its Own Reward.md
chapters.relation: Timothy Sexton argues the real Overman is not Doyle's flat 'calculating machine' but Jeremy Brett's Granada Holmes: the sneer with which he frees the Blue Carbuncle thief and the 'I am not retained by the police' outburst show him stepping beyond the herd's good-and-evil after the death of God. Brett's theatrical style, from the pivot before Lady Brackenstall in 'The Abbey Grange' to 'Gentlemen, we can do better than that' in 'The Norwood Builder', enacts Nietzsche's grand art of giving style to one's character, sublimating nihilistic dread into the pleasure of proving superiority. Where Rathbone-era Sherlocks solve crimes for truth, justice and the Victorian Way, Brett's Holmes makes the work its own reward, satisfying Nietzsche's demand that the Overman 'attain satisfaction with himself'.

chapters.file: ch08 - Education never ends Watson. It is a series of lessons with the greatest for.md
chapters.relation: J. Solomon Johnson asks whether Holmes's conclusions are knowledge or luck, walking through justified true belief with a Holmesian Gettier case (Watson rightly believing the killer was a former ship hand for the wrong reason), Moore's proof that knowledge entails belief, and Russell's stopped clock as an unsafe belief. BBC Sherlock's fake Vermeer and the 2009 film's 'resurrected' Lord Blackwood illustrate beliefs that fail safety or sensitivity across nearby possible worlds, while 'The Stock-Broker's Clerk' shows Holmes's observation of the scorched slippers making his belief sensitive. The verdict: Holmes is justified by the track record of his own expert methods, a professional billiards player rather than a beginner's-luck fluke, though real-world imitators could never rule out enough alternatives to match him.

chapters.file: ch09 - Birlstone Manor Revisited.md
chapters.relation: Fiona Tomkinson stages a Watson-Holmes dialogue in which Holmes, reworking The Valley of Fear's Birlstone Manor investigation, defines a thing as a thing of no consequence and an object as a thing transformed into a clue: the half-burned candle proving the witnesses lied, the single dumbbell used to sink Baldwin's clothes in the moat, the wedding ring and the hammer, each read through the human fear and care that moved them. A postscript has an aged Watson in 1926 discover Heidegger's newly published Being and Time and recognize his own friend's method in it: Dasein's care and being-toward-death, the directionality of equipment, and the ready-to-hand versus present-at-hand distinction, joking that Holmes might have sued Heidegger for theft of intellectual property.

chapters.file: ch10 - A Toolbox for Your Holmes.md
chapters.relation: Sami Paavola and Lauri Jaervilehto reconstruct the textbook on detection Holmes never wrote: following Jaakko Hintikka's interrogative (Socratic) model, where the right question cracks the case, as with the dog that did nothing in the night-time in 'Silver Blaze', and Peirce's triad of deduction, induction and abduction, the backward reasoning from effects to causes exemplified by the Watson-just-from-Afghanistan chain in A Study in Scarlet. They add Peirce's categories of Firstness, Secondness and Thirdness to show Holmes succeeds because he fuses imagination and reverie with fieldwork, experiment and exact inference. The chapter closes with a twelve-point practical toolbox distilled from the canon.

chapters.file: ch11 - A DOG REFLECTS THE FAMILY LIFE.md
ch12 - Final Recommendations.md
chapters.relation: Francine Sanders, a former Chicago police-misconduct investigator, rereads the 1939-46 Rathbone films (The Secret Weapon, The Spider Woman, The Woman in Green) against the hard-boiled world of Chandler and Hammett. Holmes's tea-pouring intimacy with Watson, his disguises (book peddler, roughneck sailor, bogus postman after faking his death), his puzzle-obsession rather than femme-fatale obsession with Adrea Spedding, and the closing vigil over a London where 'women can come and go in safety' mark him as the hopeful, partnered opposite of the alienated loner of noir, whose corrupt city always wins.

chapters.file: ch13 - The Postmodern Condition.md
chapters.relation: Rafe McGregor claims The Hound of the Baskervilles is not a detective story at all: the hound that never bites anyone and Holmes's failure to foresee fog on Dartmoor are, via Derrida's Of Grammatology, the aporia and re-mark where the mystery-horror hierarchy of the text deconstructs. He then applies Noel Carroll's philosophy of horror, the phosphorus-painted hound as a category-crossing monster producing fear plus disgust and Grimpen Mire as horror geography, to reclassify the novel as gothic horror alongside Frankenstein, Jekyll and Hyde and Dracula. The final section ties the book's enduring mass appeal to the postmodern condition, tracing the collapse of certainty from Nietzsche's prophecies about the end of Christian values to Derrida's claim that truth is never finally available, leaving anxiety as the novel's real engine.

chapters.file: ch14 - Chapter 8 - The Case of the Dangerous Detective.md
chapters.relation: In a Platonic dialogue, Ronald Green and D.E. Wittkower argue the detective is dangerous because knowledge itself threatens a society's ideology: Oedipus's fatal investigation, the Athenian prosecution of Socrates and Anaxagoras, and Holmes's exposure that genteel Victorian society breeds the same crimes as the slums (while the hard-boiled PI shows official authority cannot deliver), with Aristotle's catharsis re-described as ideological enforcement that teaches audiences not to question social foundations. They then widen to Indian traditions: Vyasa dividing knowledge into the Vedas like an inverted Descartes, Krishna's two paths of inquiry in the Bhagavad Gita, and the Ramayana's dharma, where Rama's trial of Sita upholds cosmic order over truth, compared with the film Raavan, to ask whether ruling by an upheld lie is the greater danger.

chapters.file: ch15 - An Eye for an Eye.md
chapters.relation: Mihaela Frunza and Anatolia Bessemer use MacIntyre's Whose Justice? Which Rationality? to frame Holmes's casual felonies, the disguised-clergyman trick on Irene Adler, freeing Captain Croker after staging a mock courtroom in 'The Abbey Grange', and compounding a felony with Isadora Klein in 'The Three Gables', as one tradition of justice among several with no neutral court of appeal. Against the police's letter-of-the-law tradition stand the criminals' own codes of retribution, above all Jefferson Hope in A Study in Scarlet letting 'the high God judge' between the poisoned and harmless pills, making Holmes and his prey mirror-image vigilantes who prefer restitution or chivalric acquittal to statutory punishment.

chapters.file: ch16 - The Game Is (and Isn’t) Afoot.md
chapters.relation: Tom Dowd argues you can never be Holmes: books and films offer only passive immersion, the flow Csikszentmihalyi describes and Marie-Laure Ryan's narrative-as-virtual-reality, with the plot pre-decided, while Holmes video games from The Riddle of the Crown Jewels to Sherlock Holmes vs. Jack the Ripper's Deduction Board supply agency and affordances for shooting and searching but offload actual deduction onto the player, who lacks Holmes's expert domain knowledge catalogued in Watson's 'his limits' list. Hence the genre's sleight of hand: Watson becomes the player's stand-in while Holmes confirms the conclusions, and BBC Sherlock's floating observation text reproduces the same trick on television.

chapters.file: ch17 - But the Contradictions! What about the Contradictions.md
chapters.relation: Ivan Wolfe asks what makes the Holmes canon (fifty-six stories and four novels) authoritative, importing the religious vocabulary of canon and apocrypha, plus Star Trek and Star Wars practice, to test borderline texts: the two Doyle tales found only in French editions ('The Man with the Watches' and 'The Lost Special'), 'The Field Bazaar', Queen Mary's Dolls' House story 'How Watson Learned the Trick', and the Gillette play that coined 'Elementary, my dear Watson'. He proposes five canon criteria (by Doyle, published in his lifetime, about Holmes, non-contradictory, prose fiction) and closes by showing Sherlockians handle internal contradictions, Watson's migrating Jezail wound and Holmes's 'Nil' philosophy grade, exactly as believers harmonize scripture: explain, deny, or await further research.

chapters.file: ch18 - I THINK YOU MIGHT WANT A LITTLE UNOFFICIAL HELP.md
ch19 - Surviving Fusion.md
chapters.relation: Amy Kind asks whether the Holmes who marries Laurie R. King's Mary Russell could still be Holmes, weighing Aristophanes' speech in Plato's Symposium (Zeus split the original spherical humans, and love seeks our lost half) against Derek Parfit's fusion case from Reasons and Persons, in which two people grow into one body, which we would all find horrifying. Against Nozick's account of love as becoming a 'we', Delaney's merger and Gaylin's 'fused identity', she deploys Marilyn Friedman's federation model, lovers as sovereign states forming a flexible third entity, to argue that Holmes and Russell's marriage survives because its fusion reshapes identity without obliterating it: his 'half a creature with two brains and four eyes' and her refusal of the nickname 'Zherlock Mary' show both lovers keeping separate selves.

chapters.file: ch20 - The Best Kind of Friend.md
chapters.relation: Ruth Tallman tests Holmes and Watson against Aristotle's requirement in the Nicomachean Ethics that perfect friendship exists only between the 'alike in excellence': since the two live by irreconcilable moral codes (Holmes's cocaine and burglaries versus Watson's clean living and law-abidingness), Aristotelian moral naturalism denies they can be true friends at all, despite the raw panic in 'The Three Garridebs' proving mutual devotion. Recasting the pair as moral pluralists with different 'good for me's, she argues Holmes is actually the better friend, an 'integrity-promoting' friend who urges Watson to stay home from the Milverton burglary to honor Watson's own code, while the proselytizing Watson, who nags about cocaine yet tags along anyway, repeatedly violates his own integrity.

chapters.file: ch21 - Defiant Male Behavior.md
chapters.relation: Julia Round traces Holmes from Baden-Powell's Scouting for Boys, which told scoutmasters to teach 'Sherlock-Holmesism', through Victorian essentialist masculinity, 'true, cold reason', stoicism under the poison darts of The Sign of the Four, yet violin, moods and the feminized domesticity of Baker Street, to argue Doyle's stories already unsettle gender essentialism. Gregory House of House, built from the same blueprint (221B, a shooter named Moriarty, a lost love named Adler, Wilson as Watson), embodies and mocks both the 1980s 'new man' and the 1990s 'new lad', cooking, soap operas, manipulation, Segways and the 'Rubik's complex', landing in Judith Butler's world where gendered behavior is a performance and masculinity is fallible, immature, and constructed.

chapters.file: ch22 - The Honorable, the Woman.md
chapters.relation: Mona Rocha and James Rocha charge that Holmes's 'deduction' is really Humean induction, and that his inductive shortcuts about women, tricking Mrs. Smith in The Sign of the Four, reading Mary Sutherland's pacing as a love affair, and dismissing Lady Frances Carfax as a 'stray chicken in a world of foxes', are hasty generalizations made dangerous by gender stereotype. Watson is worse: his 'experience of women... over many nations and three continents' reads Mary Morstan's soul off her face and grants full courtesy only to the beautiful intruder of 'The Solitary Cyclist', a feminist case study in objectification. Irene Adler's escape in 'A Scandal in Bohemia', disguising herself as a young man and outwitting the fire ruse, is Doyle's deliberate proof that treating women as a class fails, making her a proto-feminist decades before Poirot's Rossakoff or Spade's O'Shaughnessy.

chapters.file: ch23 - THERE ARE UNEXPLORED POSSIBILITIES IN YOU.md
ch24 - Wrapping Up the Case.md
chapters.relation: Don Fallis organizes the whole canon as a casebook in the epistemology of deception: why characters deceive (concealing crimes like Dr. Roylott's speckled band, committing them like John Clay's Red-Headed League tunnel, Holmes's own smoke-rocket trick on Irene Adler and his faked death at the Reichenbach Falls), how they deceive (Bell and Whaley's hide-the-truth versus show-the-false, unpacked through disguises as masking, repackaging, dazzling, mimicking, inventing and decoying), and how deception is detected, by microexpressions avant la lettre or by inconsistency, as in 'The Problem of Thor Bridge'. Along the way he sorts lying from false implicature (Inspector Baynes's 'I didn't say so'), lies of omission and bald-faced lies, invokes Kant's absolute ban on lying and Augustine's taxonomy of lies, and asks whether Holmes's belief in Moriarty's web, where the absence of evidence counts as evidence, is rational inference or self-deception.

chapters.file: ch25 - Is It All Meaningless.md
chapters.relation: Rory Kraft adopts the Great Game premise that Watson (not Doyle) wrote the memoirs and shows Watson is an untrustworthy narrator, the Jezail bullet migrating from shoulder to leg, the Tuesday March 4th murder that cannot fit the 1882 chronology, then borrows Socrates' complaint in the Phaedrus that writing 'stands in solemn silence' when questioned, so the texts cannot be cross-examined. He argues Holmes's real method is Mill's System of Logic (the Method of Residues behind 'eliminate the impossible') plus Peirce's abduction rather than deduction proper, and that Aristotle's Metaphysics ideal of truths amassing explains the Holmes brothers' knack. Failed attempts to date 'The Disappearance of Lady Frances Carfax' leave truth underdetermined, nudging toward Carnap's verdict that the unverifiable is 'meaningless' and Wittgenstein's Tractatus silence, while Derrida's 'truth is always that which can be repeated' at least settles one thing: the deerstalker was never worn.

holes.name: Abduction (inference to the best explanation)
holes.what: Peirce's third mode of inference: reasoning backwards from surprising clues to explanatory hypotheses, later formalized as inference to the best explanation.
holes.why: Chapter 10's entire reconstruction of Holmes's method (echoed in chapters 16 and 25) turns on abduction, which the taxonomy lacks alongside deduction and induction.

holes.name: Noel Carroll
holes.what: Contemporary philosopher of art and film whose The Philosophy of Horror defines horror through monsters that cross cultural categories and produce a compound of fear and disgust.
holes.why: Chapter 13 leans on Carroll's theory of horror to reclassify The Hound of the Baskervilles as gothic horror rather than detective fiction, and the taxonomy has no aesthetics-of-horror philosopher.

holes.name: Immersion, Flow and Agency in Interactive Narrative
holes.what: The cluster of concepts (flow, immersion, agency, perceived affordance) from media philosophy and game studies explaining how audiences are absorbed in narratives and act within virtual environments.
holes.why: Chapter 16 argues through exactly these concepts (Csikszentmihalyi's flow, Ryan's virtual reality, Murray's agency, Norman's affordance) that no one can be Holmes in fiction or in a video game.

holes.name: Lying and Deception (epistemology of)
holes.what: The philosophical classification of deceptive practices, lying, misleading, false implicature, omission, bald-faced lies, self-deception, together with the moral and epistemological questions of when deception is wrong and how it is detected.
holes.why: Chapter 24 is a systematic taxonomy of deception across the Holmes canon that maps only partially onto existing slugs like deontology or Frankfurt's bullshit.

holes.name: Rudolf Carnap
holes.what: Logical empiricist who argued that metaphysical statements are cognitively meaningless because they cannot be empirically verified.
holes.why: Chapter 25 closes by suggesting Holmes anticipated Carnap's dismissal of metaphysics, and the taxonomy has no logical-positivist philosopher.
